function: Hierarchical DRL jointly assigns resource blocks (DDQN), allocates BS power (TD3) and configures discrete RIS phase shifts (multi-agent DDQN) to maximize downlink sum rate (p. 1, 6-9).
system: RIS-aided downlink V2X: single-antenna BS and vehicles, passive reflecting RIS with 10-80 elements, 550 RBs in 100 MHz (5G NR, TS 38.101-1 bands), no carrier value (p. 3, 9).
method: Hierarchical reinforcement learning: DDQN for RB assignment, TD3 for power, multi-agent DDQN with shared network (CTDE) for RIS phases; event-triggered updates, initialized from analytical solution (p. 6-9).
data_channel: Custom simulator: Rayleigh BS-user, Rician BS-RIS and RIS-user links, path-loss exponent 2.2, Doppler, Poisson-placed moving vehicles; no 3GPP model, public data or measurements (p. 3-4, 8).
test_conditions: No separate train/test split stated; agents train over episodes and results are swept over power, RIS elements, velocity, SNR and user distribution; no unseen-condition test stated (p. 9-12).
baselines: Non-learned: analytical lower bound (authors' own), no-RIS. Learned: PPO-based [49] and DDPG-based [50] joint optimizers, plus the authors' DRL-only variant (p. 9-10).
metrics: System sum rate (Mbps) versus power, RIS elements, velocity, SNR, RIS height and distance; sum-rate CDF; normalized reward and loss over episodes; trigger counts (p. 10-12).
complexity: Complexity orders: analytical O((WKT+N)^3), DDQN O(T_RB|A_RB|M_RB), TD3 O(T_P|A_P|(2M_C+M_A)), RIS DDQN O(N T_Theta|A_Theta|M_Theta); overall order in Eq. 54; no runtime (p. 9, 14).
q1_support: p. 3: "the channel between the BS and vehicular user-i follows Rayleigh fading" (BS-RIS and RIS-user links are Rician); custom simulator, 3GPP TS 38.101-1 is cited only for operating bands, no TR 38.901 or measured data.
q2_support: p. 9: "is varied from 2 to 100 to explore different traffic densities" (users) and RIS elements "which vary from 10 to 80 in the simulations"; these are sweeps, and the paper never states that a model trained in one setting is tested in another.
q3_support: p. 10: "Lower Bound: This benchmark uses the optimal values from the iterative optimizer of this work" (non-learned) and "PPO-based Algorithm [49]", "DDPG-based Algorithm [50]" (learned), all compared on sum rate in Figs. 6-9.
q4_support: p. 9: "The overall complexity is:" Eq. (54) gives O((WKT+N)^3) plus DDQN and TD3 terms in training steps, action-space size and network size; derivations in Appendix C, p. 14.
q5_support: p. 9: "parameters are provided in Table II"; the channels come from a custom simulator and no code or data link or DOI is given.
notes: Area 3: the learned RIS phase configuration is trained jointly with RB assignment and BS power (main metric sum rate), so it passes above_phy by the joint rule; single-antenna link but with RIS. The non-learned baseline (q3) is the authors' own analytical lower bound (p. 10); the no-RIS and DRL-only benchmarks are variants of the method and not counted. Fig. 10 (p. 12) compares uniform and Poisson user placement, but the paper does not say agents were trained on one and tested on the other. Table II (p. 8) read as an image.
